Q: How to change the color of a specific word from user in "input()" A:

While you can alter the colours in the terminal using a library such as curses or termcolor, it is more challenging than the basic input function provided by python.

I have an example here for you, using curses but it could be accomplished easier in your own window, rather than the terminal, using for example tkinter or one of the python qt libraries.

Essentially you will need to read the input from the user, see if it was a match to any of your special words, then go replace the special word with the coloured variant. The version I have here is very minimal, it doesn't support backspace and doesn't check if your special word is buried in a larger word and so on, but might be enough to get you started, if you choose to go this route.

import curses

RED_PAIR = 1
BLUE_PAIR = 2

def main(stdscr: curses.window):
    # This must be called before you can initialize the colour pairs
    curses.start_color()
    # Choose a couple random colours
    curses.init_pair(RED_PAIR, curses.COLOR_RED, curses.COLOR_BLACK)
    curses.init_pair(BLUE_PAIR, curses.COLOR_CYAN, curses.COLOR_BLACK)
    # Create a lookup of all the special words that should be highlighted
    special_words = {
        'class': curses.color_pair(RED_PAIR),
        'def': curses.color_pair(BLUE_PAIR)
    }
    # Clear the window
    stdscr.clear()
    # Look forever, which can exited using ctrl-c
    while True:
        # Refresh the screen
        stdscr.refresh()
        # Get the next user input
        new_char = stdscr.getkey()
        # Put that in the screen
        stdscr.addstr(new_char)
        # Refresh so that the cursor moves and the text is drawn to the screen
        stdscr.refresh()
        # Get the cursor position it can be reset after all these function calls
        y, x = curses.getsyx()
        # Check each special word, looking for a match
        for special_word, colour_pair in special_words.items():
            # First, check the length to make sure there is enough space
            char_len = len(special_word)
            if x < char_len:
                # Not enough space for this word
                continue
            # Grab the characters to check
            match_candidate = stdscr.instr(y, x - char_len, char_len).decode()
            if match_candidate == special_word:
                # There was a match, set the colour and add the text on top of it
                stdscr.attron(colour_pair)
                stdscr.addstr(y, x - char_len, special_word)
                stdscr.attroff(colour_pair)
        # Reset the cursor, all the above functions move it around
        stdscr.move(y, x)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    curses.wrapper(main)

Q: What are Rust Crates A:

Typically crate is a single folder containing all of your code and how to build and/or run it. It contains src folder together with Cargo.toml file, tests, examples, build artifacts, everything. It is a project. Which can also depend on other crates/projects. That's all. Then there are variations (like workspace), but that's the main idea.

Hmm, this does not really support your claim – on the contrary:

<embed>

[…] From inside an embedded SVG or HTML document you can reach the parent with:

parent = window.parent.document;

So, if that is possible for SVG, why would it not be possible for PDF? Respectively, for an XSS exploit in a PDF viewer e.g.? Still, we're talking about defense-in-depth, I know obviously it's browser's responsibility not to have vulnerabilities in their PDF viewer but well… you never know.

And yes, CSP applies to the whole page, the sandbox attributes has basically the same properties and applies only to the iframe, so it can be much more limited.

The question stands: Does the same-origin policy differentiate an embed/object from the page atop?. I just noticed the linked MDN site says:

Here are some examples of resources which may be embedded cross-origin:

  • External resources embedded with <object> and <embed>.

But I guess this only means/applies, you can theoretically embed a PDF from a foreign website (which then would have cross-origin applied, which is good).

Q: wxTreeCtrl::SelectItem is too slow. What to do? A:

You should definitely freeze the tree while doing it, but 10000 is a too big number of items to select at once in any reasonable scenario. For the trees with such number of items, you would typically delay doing anything with the items until the parent node is expanded (including even adding them to the tree), so the real fix is to only select the items the currently shown items and wait until wxEVT_TREE_ITEM_EXPANDING and only then select all the items under the parent.
